title: Developer Runbook Cards: micro-scenarios for API pairing, session replay & tool-mapping
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Create a compact set of 'Runbook Cards' — single-screen, reusable illustration + copy assets that demonstrate 6 realistic developer micro-scenarios for the API/SDK quickstart. Each card is an asset that pairs a short narrative, a screenshot or micro-animation frame, and a recommended code snippet (JS + Python). The aim is to reduce cognitive load in the onboarding doc by offering scenario-driven entry points (e.g., 'First authenticated streaming session', 'Ephemeral key rotate + resume', 'Tool call: document search -> call tool -> inject result', 'Session replay for debugging', 'Fallback to quantized model under high load', 'Dedicated capacity handshake example'). Deliver high-fidelity Figma components, export-ready PNG/SVG sprites, one animated Lottie prototype for the streaming timeline, and copy variations (short, medium, long) for doc, console tooltip, and email drip. Consider accessibility (color contrast, screenreader labels), localization (short copy variants for i18n), and token metrics microchart to show cost/latency tradeoffs.
deliverables: 12 static exports (PNG @2x) and 6 SVG master exports
1 Lottie animation (streaming timeline + prefix cache visual)
Code snippets (JS, Python) with copy-paste ready examples for each card
Copy variants (short/medium/long) and microcopy for console tooltip
Accessibility pass notes and contrast tokens list
Handoff package (Figma file link, asset zip, README for devs)
acceptance_criteria: All 6 cards exist as reusable Figma components with documented variants
Each card has a verified code snippet that runs against the sandbox API (QA checked)
Static exports match the spec sizes and are optimized (SVGs minified, PNGs @2x)
Lottie animation tested in prototype playback and attached in handoff zip
Design review approved by PM (Marco Ruiz) and Eng owner (Jia Huang)
Accessibility checklist completed: contrast, keyboard order, alt text
design_notes: Chosen micro-scenario format because metrics show higher completion when users see concrete example flows vs abstract 'getting started' steps.
Avoided heavy metaphors (e.g., 'pipeline illustrations') to keep asset library reusable across SDK, Console, and Email.
Motion should be subtle: streaming heartbeat + progressive token meter; avoid autoplay in embedded docs to respect user bandwidth.
Trade-off: single-frame clarity vs step-by-step micro-interaction — decided to produce both a primary static hero for docs and a short Lottie for the streaming card.
Session replay card will use anonymized fake data; engineering to provide a sanitized sample log for screenshot consistency.
Localization: keep primary copy under 80 characters for mobile variants; provide a fallback longer copy for desktop only.
